# *Preface*
### TO THE
## READER

It has been many years now, Dear Reader, that one hears of nothing but quarrels and disputes throughout all of <term>Christendom</term><note>The collective community of Christians or Christian nations.</note>, concerning the articles of faith: for this reason, so many <term>Colleges</term> and <term>Universities</term> have been established in the world, and such a great number of weighty books have been written regarding the various opinions in matters of <term>Theology</term><note>Original: "Godts-geleertheit," literally meaning "God-learnedness."</note>; so many <term>Councils</term><note>Formal assemblies of church leaders meant to settle matters of doctrine.</note> have been assembled; so many high Teachers have been brought together in our times, and with such great care, diligence, effort, and expense: and yet, until now, one has not been able to prevent discord and division. The schisms and disputes within Christendom are greater today than ever before. How many contradictory opinions are there among the theologians? How many persons have separated themselves from the <term>Roman Church</term> in order to uphold their own opinions? How many...

<summary>In this preface, the author laments the persistent and growing religious divisions within the Christian world, noting that despite the proliferation of universities, theological texts, and church councils, unity remains elusive.</summary>
<keywords>Christendom, religious disputes, theology, Church Councils, Roman Catholic Church, education, schism, faith</keywords>

*knowing what <term>Philosophy</term> or <term>Theology</term> mean.*

She possesses in substance, perfectly, all the sciences, without having learned them through any human means.

# FIRST LETTER.

## To a faithful Friend, explaining to him in confidence that all contemporary <term>huidendaegsche: referring to the established religious doctrines of the 17th century</term> Theology contradicts the wisdom of the Holy Spirit, and that those who believe themselves to be the wisest in Divine mysteries are the most ignorant.

My Lord,

I can see nothing else in contemporary Theology than that it has a completely perverse sense; and that it contradicts the truths that God makes known to me. I have never attended the Schools <note>The "Schools" refers to formal university training in theology, which was then restricted to men and focused on Aristotelian logic and scholasticism</note>; but when I hear our Theologians explain their thoughts and reveal their sentiments, then I find them so contrary to the truths of God that I can agree with them in nothing. ## What true Miracles are. ##

[They have been] filled with **Divine Wisdom**; and after them, so many **Holy Persons**, though ignorant in letters <note>Meaning they were illiterate or lacked formal academic training.</note>, have meanwhile possessed the wisdom of the **Holy Spirit**: so many **Anchorites** <term>Anchorite: a religious recluse who lives in isolation to focus on prayer and penance.</term> in the deserts, so many simple shepherds in the fields, so many humble daughters have been filled with **Divine Wisdom**, without other means than that of a pure conscience.

Do you now wish to limit the grace of the **Holy Spirit**, and prevent Him from doing so any longer? This belongs to no man to do. They may judge whatever pleases them: but they cannot prevent the **Holy Spirit** from extending the influence of His graces directly over simple souls without the intervention of men; and causing them to speak a language that shall be understood by all peoples of the world, for those who may have tasted this **Divine Wisdom** in any way. The author here personifies the soul as being "possessed" or inhabited by the Spirit.</note>, because they are all supernatural and divine matters. If one sees a person who is permitted to enjoy the pleasures of the flesh, the luxuries of taste, and of the other senses, and who willingly abstains from them in order to please God more; this person performs a **miracle**, because he does a thing that surpasses nature. Likewise, he who has wealth, lawfully obtained, and yet does not wish to use it nor serve himself with it except for simple necessity, living rich as if he were poor; this is a great miracle in our time. Likewise, when a person of high status, who could be fitly served and honored, disdains these honors and services to follow Jesus Christ, preferring to remain unknown and even to serve others rather than be served. All these things are miraculous, because they strive against nature and overcome it.

All these true miracles are to be desired and deserve to be closely examined; and when these can be found in a person, then one must demand no other miracles from them, because their entire life is then full of miracles and powerful virtues. One will certainly find in such a soul all the requirements of love <note>original: "liefde." # What true Miracles are.

I have elaborated somewhat on all these matters so that later, my Lord, you may better take your measure to distinguish and know where the Spirit of God might be; and that you should not let yourself be deceived by false appearances, placing your trust in outward miracles, which serve only the unbelieving and the ignorant. It is not that I wish to exclude true miracles from the souls who love God; for they would surely perform as many of them in this present time as the **Apostles** did in their lives, if it were not necessary for the glory of God, who will always do the will of those who love Him at all times and in all places. But I have said all these things to make you see that it is the least grace that God bestows upon a faithful, believing soul in this world to have the gift of **Prophecy**, or of performing miracles; and that these things should not be esteemed in comparison to the faith and the love that unites souls with God. ### That God Gave But a Single Commandment

This single commandment was given in Adam to all people, and God would never have commanded anything else to anyone in particular than only this: to depend on Him <note>original: "aen te hangen"; this implies a sense of clinging to, or being devotedly attached to God</note>; by means of which everyone could have enjoyed with delight everything that God had created for them. And just as God is unchangeable, so He could never change this institution in Himself, and never demand anything else from all people who are born of Adam and will be born. He created them all to take His pleasure with them, and not to subject them to strict and difficult laws; nor to make them His slaves under the burden of various orders or commandments, giving them nothing but a single one, so that through love they might always acknowledge the benefit of their God, and that this knowledge would make them depend entirely on Him alone in all things, seeing as they have received everything from Him—their being, life, body, and **understanding** <term>verstand: the faculty of reason and the intellect</term>, the soul, and the **eternity** which they expect.

And this second commandment was given to all people in Adam, to the end that every one of them might recognize the miseries into which this failure to depend on God <note>original: "niet aen Godt te hangen"; the author uses this phrase throughout to describe the loss of a soul's natural attachment to its Creator</note> had brought them: of tilling the earth and suffering its curse, as well as the curse of all the other creatures who had risen up against man since he had abandoned his dependence on his God; for previously, they were all subject to him. From which it follows that this second commandment of God does not proceed directly from God <note>The author suggests this law was "incidental" or reactive, rather than part of God's original, perfect plan for humanity</note>; but it is given as a consequence, by reason of sin, through the great love that God bears for man. He did not wish to let him perish, as he had well deserved; but He gives him only a law through which he might return to depending on his God.

### That God gave but one single Commandment

Through this means, He gives to mankind this entire beautiful world, to enjoy and use it in abundance; He sustains man within his body, giving of Himself to serve as the sustenance and spiritual delights of the soul. What great ingratitude it is to refuse to submit to a commandment so good, so beneficial, and so profitable for humanity, who—acting as enemies of their own happiness—rebel against this divine arrangement.

In the meantime, God never changes this order, and will never change it, having established it from the beginning. He can never give humanity any Law other than this: to depend upon Him <note>original: "aen hem te hangen"; literally "to hang on him," a common 17th-century mystical term for total spiritual dependence and constant adherence to God’s will.</note>, which is so reasonable that even the natural senses should not resist it. For even the animals recognize their benefactors; yet man, making himself more bestial than they, demonstrates his ingratitude by refusing to depend on anything but his own will.

Meanwhile God—ever unchangeable and persevering in His original decrees—does not change His intention to find His delight <note>original: "lust"; referring to the divine joy or "pleasure" God takes in being united with the human soul.</note> among mankind. Seeing that they have become rebellious against this dependence on Him, He calls them back: first, through the path of penance <term>penance: original "boete," referring here to the life of toil and repentance assigned to Adam after the Fall</term> which He laid upon Adam; secondly, through the Law of Moses; and thirdly, through the Law of the Gospel. It is not that God has need...

<meta>This page continues the discussion from page 59/60 regarding the "essential law" of human dependence on God. ->[that He] gave to mankind.<-

...either penance <term>penance: here referring to the "path of toil" or restorative suffering</term>, or the Law of Moses, nor even the Evangelical Law <note>original: "Evangelische Wet"; referring to the teachings of the New Testament</note>; but rather, it is that humanity needs these things to return to this rightful adherence <note>original: "aenhangen"; the mystical concept of the soul "clinging to" or "hanging upon" God's will.</note> to their God. In His mercy, God reveals through this first and second Law, and also this last one which Jesus Christ taught us, those things that have drawn us away from this adherence. # SIXTH LETTER.

*That a soul taught immediately by the Holy Spirit has no need to read anything, or to learn from men, which would much sooner hinder than help her in understanding the truth of God.*

# EIGHTH LETTER.

->To the same.<-

*Explaining to him what certain signs there are to recognize the true Prophets through the Scriptures themselves, and how many false ones have arisen in these days who deceive others and themselves through their arrogance.*

My Lord,

I come by this letter to answer your third question, in which you say that for many years now your soul has been troubled by a burden <note>original: "swarigheid"; meaning a spiritual weight, difficulty, or persistent worry.</note>; seeing in these times in which we live so many persons who call themselves Prophets and Teachers <term>Leeraers: spiritual instructors, doctors of theology, or ministers</term>, and bring forth so many teachings; each saying they are sent by God, and that one must believe them. ### Signs to Recognize the True [Prophets]

Just as **God** is good, just, and true, so shall he also be who truly knows and loves Him. If one sees anything in these **Prophets** contrary to the goodness, justice, and truth of **God**, then one must never believe that they have been sent by Him, because he who is His friend is always transformed into Him, and precisely shares in these three qualities of **Goodness**, **Justice** <note>original: "gerechtigheit"; can also be translated as "righteousness" in a theological context.</note>, and **Truth**, bringing forth the same through all his works.

## NINTH LETTER.

*To a learned and godly person, who wondered why people continue to grow worse even as Churches, Sermons, Prayers, and other religious duties daily multiply; showing him that true worship does not consist in the splendor and absurdities of external rituals, but in the lifting up of one's spirit to God, to worship Him in spirit and in truth.* <note>This heading references John 4:24, a cornerstone text for 17th-century mystics who prioritized internal experience over outward ceremony.</note>

# TENTH LETTER.

->To the same.<-

*Explaining to him the abuses that now exist in all Holy matters, which proves that the **abomination of desolation** <note>A biblical reference (Matthew 24:15) used by Bourignon to signify that the institutional Church has become a site of spiritual ruin.</note> is in the Holy Place, and that it is almost time to **flee from Judea.** <note>In Bourignon’s mystical geography, "Judea" often represents the visible, institutional Church. To "flee Judea" means to leave these structures to find God in spirit and truth.</note>*

My Lord,

Since you desire that I should give my opinion on all the points of the Christian Religion in which I observe abuses; I am willing to reveal my thoughts to you on this matter, although they are still secret, and few persons have the capacity to receive them well; because everyone flatters themselves and does not want to hear the reproving truth. Yet it is nonetheless useful and beneficial for all those who are eager to please God and to strive for their eternal **salvation** <term>saligheid: refers to both the state of being saved and the enduring happiness of the soul in heaven</term>, of whom I believe you to be one: and although it will fall somewhat hard upon you to hear things that conflict with your pious feelings, and against what you have previously learned and taught to others; you shall nonetheless be overcome by the truth, and be obliged to say with sorrow, as well as I, that we have fallen greatly away from the faith- <note>Original catchword: *ve,*; completing the Dutch word *geloove* (faith)</note>

# ELEVENTH LETTER.

## To the same person,

->*Explaining to him that humans, by loving themselves, cannot love God.*<-

My Lord,

I have great pity to see and hear that men say and believe they love **God**, while they love nothing but themselves; whereas the **Commandment** <note>Referring to the "Great Commandment" found in Matthew 22:37: "Love the Lord your God with all your heart..."</note> to love God is so essentially necessary for **salvation** <note>Dutch: *saligheid* — the state of eternal grace or being saved.</note> that no one could be saved without fulfilling it. The Law of the **Gospel** is contained in this Commandment alone—to love God—in which true love consists. But people nowadays no longer love God because they love themselves, and these two loves conflict too much with one another to be able to exist together in one heart. Fire would much sooner exist in water, finding fewer contradictions there. Yet it is such a highly necessary Commandment that one shall love God with all one's heart, with all one's soul, and with all one's strength; otherwise, one could not be saved. It is not a single step <meta>catchword: of</meta>

<summary>In this opening of the eleventh letter, the author argues that the fundamental requirement for salvation is the love of God, which is currently being stifled by humanity's prevailing self-love. She asserts that these two forms of love are as incompatible as fire and water, yet loving God with one's entire being remains the absolute core of the Gospel.</summary>

*That the Commandment to love God, &c.*

of voluntary perfection, but a Commandment for all Persons who wish to enter into **Paradise**: and no one shall enter therein through any other gate, **God** having so ordained it from the beginning of the world: and those who do not fulfill his Commandments cannot be **saved** <note>Dutch: *salig* — meaning to be blessed or to achieve eternal life.</note>, or God would not be God; because he would not be God if he were changeable, as men imagine—believing that human habits bring about a change in God's eyes. It is a great deception, and very deadly darkness, in which we currently find ourselves, that no one keeps this commandment, and yet the whole world wants to be saved: such a terrible misunderstanding, which causes almost the whole world to perish, the majority of **Christians** dying with the imagination of their salvation, even though they have not loved God with their whole hearts: and thus they descend insensibly into **Hell**, the gate of Paradise being closed to all those who shall not have loved God with their whole heart. For it is a strict and necessary commandment: the **Evangelical counsels** <term>Evangelical counsels: Spiritual recommendations from the Gospels—such as voluntary poverty, chastity, and obedience—that are traditionally seen as paths to perfection rather than requirements for all.</term> are means to keep that commandment; but are not solely necessary for salvation: for they who can attain to this love of God without renouncing all they possess are not obliged to reject all their belongings, being able to make use of their goods, even to maintain this love of **God**—

### That the Commandment to love God, &c.

[...to maintain] it. He who possesses this love is not obligated to leave **Father**, **Mother**, **Brother**, **Sister**, and all others; nor to give his cloak to the one who takes his coat; because all these things are only for **counsel** <note>The author refers here to the "Evangelical counsels" mentioned on the previous page—actions that are spiritually beneficial but not strictly required for all believers.</note>, and they serve us as means. But the love of **God** is of the commandment, necessary for **salvation** <note>Dutch: *saligheit* — meaning to be blessed or to achieve eternal life.</note>; without the keeping of which, no one can ever be saved: and all those who speak to the contrary are **Antichrists**; who set themselves against the teachings of **Jesus Christ**, indeed, against the decree of the **Holy Trinity**, which has established this so firmly, from the first commandment onwards, that He gave to men. 

Is there any human or hellish power that can change that? Must one not firmly love **God** with one's whole heart, or go to **Hell**? This is so certain and sure, that no rational **creatures** can doubt it; unless it were the wickedness of men who are held in high esteem, and who bear the name of **Servants of Jesus Christ** on earth, who misled and deceived the common people; making so many interpretations and declarations regarding this commandment, that they cause it to disappear from their spirit; or at least they disguise it in such a way, that everyone imagines they love **God**, when they love themselves, their **riches**, and the pleasures of the world. 

Is this not indeed a fine compromise? <note>The author is being sarcastic here, mocking the idea that one can balance a love for the world with a love for God.</note> The love of **God** cannot exist in a soul that loves the luxuries and riches of the world;

# ...is necessary for salvation.

...no more than fire can remain in water without being extinguished: because one opposite always infallibly drives out its contrary. If you love **God**, you will not love the world, since all the laws of the world are set directly against the laws of **God**. Meanwhile, all the children of the world say that they love **God**. And how would it be possible to love the truth without hating lies, or to love righteousness <note>original: *gerechtigheit* — this term implies both moral uprightness and divine justice.</note> without having an aversion to the deceit with which the world is filled? Who can love poverty without despising riches; or humility, without fleeing vain glory? These are all conflicting things, where one must drive out its opposite. 

What means is there, then, to love both **God** and the world? Must not the strongest get the upper hand? Can they remain together for long? One needs only natural judgment <note>The author appeals to common sense or "natural reason" here, suggesting the logic is self-evident.</note> to judge "no," and consequently to condemn all those who say they love **God** while they love the world; because infallibly, he who loves **God** hates the world: and if one loves the world, then he hates **God**. For one cannot serve two masters without being unfaithful to one or the other, says **Jesus Christ**. The love of **God**, coming to take its seat in a soul, drives out from it al—

—l that **God** is not, and causes the soul to imperceptibly lay aside all earthly affections; and if any earthly affections have possessed a soul, then the love of **God** is driven out from there, and it cannot remain alongside them. And as a certain test, to know whether one loves **God**, everyone must examine all the powers of their soul <note>The author refers to the traditional "three powers of the soul": Memory, Understanding, and Will.</note>, to see toward what they are directed; whether the memory thinks of nothing but **God**; whether the understanding <note>original: *verstand* — the faculty used for reasoning and discernment.</note> is busy with nothing else than to provide for His honor; whether the will does not press itself except to please Him. 

These are infallible testimonies that one loves **God**: but if all these things are busy to please the world, or to obtain riches or honors; it is a certain sign that one does not love **God**: because the love of **God** consumes earthly desires <note>original: *begeerlijkheden* — this refers to worldly cravings or lusts.</note>, and kills all sensory movements and passions, and that so powerfully, that if the same love did not sustain the soul and the body, the sensory drive could not maintain them in their essence: in this way self-love ends when the love of **God** reigns. 

The beauty of this love makes everything seem ugly that is outside of **God**; its goodness makes one regard as evil all that is found outside of this love; and all created things seem to be nothing when one possesses this **All** <note>The "All" (Dutch: *het Al*) is a mystical term for God as the totality of being, against which the "nothingness" of the created world is compared.</note>. This is that He has made His love inseparable from the love of one's **neighbor** <note>original: *naeften* — referring to the biblical command to "love thy neighbor."</note>, so that one cannot exist without the love of the neighbor when one loves **God**; no more than the **Sun** can exist without light; and one cannot love one's neighbor without doing him good, which is the visible working of love. If one then loved **God**, as one claims to do, one would, by that same consequence, love one's neighbor as oneself; and one would see all Christians heartily loving one another: but on the contrary, one sees among them nothing but cruelties, deceits, and perversions, hating one another, without any love. # That the Commandment to love God

[people] not [deceive themselves], when they say that one can certainly reach salvation <note>original: *falig* — referring to being "saved" or attaining eternal blessedness.</note> by living as people do nowadays? These are false convictions, leading the entire world to damnation: some through their own wicked deeds, others through ignorance, allowing themselves to believe they are keeping the Commandments of God while doing the exact opposite. I see no true Christians on Earth anymore: they are nothing but false masks, displaying what they are not before God. For to be a true Christian, one must follow the fundamental rules of the Gospel; and no one sees that. It seems that living like the Christians of the Early Church <note>original: *eerfte Kerk* — the primitive Christian community as described in the New Testament, often idealized in later centuries as a model of perfect devotion.</note> is considered a folly, simply because we no longer live in those times. Terrible misunderstandings! To believe that the passage of time has changed the Laws of God. Would He have left His teaching on Earth for none but those first Christians? Or perhaps He did it for the Turks <note>In the 17th century, "Turks" was the standard European term for all Muslims.</note>, Heathens, and Idol-worshippers who were to come after them? They have not been instructed in it; how could they possibly uphold those same laws when they do not know them? If this Teaching of the Gospel had not been established for anyone but the first Christians, it would not have been necessary to set it down in writing; since they had heard it from the very mouth of Jesus Christ Himself, they could easily have remembered it and passed it on to those who were to [carry it] until a determined time.

We see our neighbor just as blind as we are ourselves; and we think that everything must go this way, because it has become a common practice to run in a crowd along the path to **Hell**. Everyone follows the procession, without thinking any more of the Law of God; and much less that one must uphold the **Teaching of the Gospel** to be a true Christian. Thus, people live like **Atheists** <note>In the 17th century, "Atheist" often referred to "practical atheism"—living as if God does not exist or has no influence on human affairs, rather than a modern philosophical denial of God's existence.</note>, who do not believe that there is a God; indeed, even much worse. # That the Commandment to Love God Is Necessary for Salvation.

...[even if] one gave [all one's possessions], and handed over his body to be burned; indeed, even if one had the gift of prophecy, understood all sciences, and could even move mountains, it would all be of no help if one does not have love. And for fear that one might not know what love is, he <note>Referring to St. Paul the Apostle.</note> continues by explaining it, saying:

> Love is patient; it is kind, and does no one wrong; love is not willful <note>original: *moedwillig* — in this context, meaning acting out of self-will or being easily provoked.</note>, it is not puffed up; it is not ambitious; it does not seek its own advantages; it is not bitter; it thinks no evil; it does not rejoice in injustice, but rejoices in the truth. It bears all things; it believes all things; it hopes all things; it endures all things. Love never fails, even if prophecies should cease, and tongues fall silent, and knowledge be destroyed.

These are all the words of the Apostle, in which he points out to us what love is; having well foreseen that in these present times, no one would truly know what love might be. For people think they are in love <note>The author uses *liefde* here in the sense of the theological virtue of Charity (*Caritas*), which is a selfless, divine love rather than mere emotion.</note> when they do not murder, do not steal, nor commit any coarse material sin, and when they bear the name of Christians, performing Christian duties outwardly; which is nevertheless nothing but the apron and the mask of a Christian. For even if, he says, you gave so many alms, and distributed your goods to the poor, you would not for that reason have love, if you did not simultaneously have the love of God:

# That the Commandment to Love God

...and if you hand over your body to be burned, without this divine love, it would not help you; and even less to possess all sciences <note>In this period, "sciences" (*wetenschappen*) refers more broadly to systematic knowledge or academic learning rather than just the modern physical sciences.</note> and gifts; yes, even such a great faith that you could move mountains; all this is vain without the love of God. Such persons are very uncommon, and yet they still could not be certain of being saved if they did not also have the love of God. How then can those promise themselves salvation who have none of these gifts or qualities; but on the contrary are hardened against the poor and so preoccupied with self-love that they cannot patiently suffer even the bite of a flea, much less a word of contradiction? Meanwhile, they live and die in the confidence of their salvation because they see almost no one else doing otherwise—the blindness being so general. This is what makes our times so dangerous. For the words of the Apostle are true, as are those of Jesus Christ:

### [that the Commandment to love God] is necessary for Salvation.

...may enjoy their desires? And how few rejoice in the truth, especially when it rebukes them in any way! No one wishes to hear it anymore, everyone wanting to be flattered in their own faults. The Apostle <note>Saint Paul, referencing 1 Corinthians 13</note> continues, saying that love bears all things, and hopes all things, to show that the love of God gives such strength that one bears all kinds of evils for His sake. It is this love that gave strength to **St. Lawrence** <note>Saint Lawrence was a 3rd-century deacon of Rome who, according to tradition, was martyred by being roasted on a gridiron; he famously told his executioners to "turn him over" as he was done on one side.</note> to mock his oppressor in the midst of the glowing coals that roasted his body; and which gave all the **Martyrs** the will to die for **Jesus Christ**, and to endure all kinds of pains with joy for His name. The same love believes what is true, without contradiction: hopes in all the promises of God, without any fear or lack of faith. # Message to the Reader.

I HAVE noticed, dear Reader, that the Devil is eager to extinguish the light that God has caused to rise in these dark times; for he hinders, through so many various means, the publication of the writings of Antoinette Bourignon. God had raised up the person of Christian de Cort, Director of Nordstrand <note>Nordstrand is an island off the coast of North Frisia. Christian de Cort (d. 1669) was a Roman Catholic priest and close associate of Bourignon who attempted to establish a religious community there. The project failed due to immense debt and legal opposition.</note>, to seek out and collect these, as they are very salutary and advantageous writings for the salvation of souls who seek Christian perfection: but the malicious, in order to hinder these godly intentions, have by another way rendered the said De Cort powerless to carry this out, having held him for six months in a harsh prison, where he contracted so many damp vapors, catarrhs, and cold chills <note>The original Dutch "sijnkingen en koude vallingen" refers to 17th-century medical understandings of respiratory ailments and "fluxes" of bodily humors caused by exposure to damp, cold environments.</note> from the autumn air, that he died a short time thereafter, nevertheless leaving behind to us several Letters written by the hand of the said A. B. <note>A. B. is an abbreviation for Antoinette Bourignon.</note>, both to him and to many other persons, which can greatly enlighten all people of good will. Through these, one can discover the good and the evil of all matters, so that one may beware of evil and follow the good. For this reason, I have decided to bring these to light, so that

doubting whether I should submit to the examination of men writings composed by the Holy Spirit. <note>Bourignon believed her writings were not her own thoughts but were dictated directly by God; therefore, she felt that submitting them to a human "Overseer" or censor for approval was a form of blasphemy.</note> And seeing that I could not bring them to light there without danger of reprimand or punishment, I decided for that reason to come to Amsterdam, as to a free place to do so, intending afterwards to travel even further: but occurring events have prevented me from doing what I had intended; having not yet begun to print the said booklet, nor to travel further, because of the great dangers and shipwrecks that were heard of here when we thought to depart: so that I have remained in Amsterdam since the month of December 1667 until now, where I still am by the very will of God, who constantly works in my soul for His honor and the salvation of others.

# Religion is Inconstancy <note>Bourignon uses the word *ongestadigheit* (instability/inconstancy) to suggest that outward religious labels are shifting and unreliable compared to the constancy of the Holy Spirit.</note>

[possessed] by Jesus Christ; and to follow the works that He did while on earth, in order to give us an example. It matters little what one calls our Religion, if our heart is not religious—that is to say, bound or reborn in the spirit of Jesus Christ; otherwise, we shall no more be saved in the Roman Church than in any other. One must indeed be a Christian to be saved, otherwise no Religions shall save us; because Jesus Christ is the only way that leads to life.

And to answer what you ask me, whether I have changed my Religion; I answer you absolutely no—indeed, that I shall never change. I was born in the Catholic, Apostolic, and Roman Church, in the spirit of Jesus Christ; and I wish so to live and die. I do not know what could make me change, since I find nothing better. I had never in my life been in any place outside the obedience of Rome: Amsterdam is the first place where I hear other Religions spoken of. I still do not know to this day on what all these differences of beliefs are grounded, having never associated with any person whom we call a <term>heretic</term> <note>original: *ketter*. In the 17th century, this was a standard Catholic term for Protestants.</note>, and even less having read their controversial writings <note>Refers to polemical or "disputation" books where different sects argued over doctrine.</note>, about which I have no desire to ask—

### The Changing of

[to ask]; and I have also not yet heard a single one of their **sermons**, in more than two years that I have been here. Upon my arrival, I rented a house behind some **warehouses** in a place where there were six different dwellings, which six houses were inhabited by people of six different **religions**. Initially, I could not understand this, which seemed so strange to me, and I almost felt a desire to go once to each of these meetings to know what was done there; but God afterwards took this desire away from me, and let me see that nothing therein was well-founded. For this reason, I have never been in any of these meetings, nor have I entered any of their churches.

My neighbors have left me in peace, because there is great freedom of **conscience** here; everyone lives without reproach in the belief they think best. I remained unknown for some time, without speaking to anyone; but due to an illness that befell me, I was forced to summon a <term>physician</term> <note>original: *Genees-meefter*. Many will say that the truth is in the **Holy Scripture**; which I acknowledge and certainly believe: but I also know that the same Spirit that caused it to be written must still give the understanding <note>original: "verstand," referring to spiritual insight rather than mere intellectual comprehension</note> of it; otherwise, each person will understand it in their own way and according to their own opinion, shaping it according to their passions and personal feelings, and not according to the true meaning.

# Better to pray for the grace of God,

...are capable of receiving other lights than those they imagine they have; and thus their lights become darkness, and those they still seem to possess are taken away from them through the conceit of their spirit and their high opinion of themselves.

### IX. LETTER.

# On the true virtue.

A person who is reborn in the Spirit of Jesus Christ <term>Spirit of Jesus Christ: "Geeſt Jeſu Chriſti," referring to the internal presence of the divine rather than mere religious observance</term> has no need to occupy themselves with the dealings and commerce of the world: they strive only to gather treasures where the worms do not gnaw through them, nor the thieves steal <note>A reference to the Gospel of Matthew 6:20. Bourignon frequently uses biblical imagery to contrast spiritual wealth with material greed.</note>. Meanwhile, those who immerse themselves in the dealings of the world gain as much as is possible for them; and they still want people to believe that they are reborn in the Spirit of Jesus Christ, although all their actions are entirely contrary and opposed to those of Jesus Christ and his spirit. 

For although they speak humbly and maintain themselves in humble gestures <note>original: "gebeerten." This refers to outward physical displays of piety, such as bowing the head or specific ways of standing or walking associated with religious groups like the Mennonites of Bourignon's time.</note>, they meanwhile have a very proud heart when they want people to believe that they are reborn; and they would take it quite poorly if I were to say that they are not. 

This comes from the fact that they do not know true and genuine virtue <term>virtue: original "deugt." For Bourignon, virtue is an inner light and transformation, not a set of social rules.</term> well, and place the foundation of it in outward things, by which they deceive themselves, or wish to deceive others, and appear before the eyes of men as what they are not before God, but only in a false humility. For Jesus Christ has not commanded us to be humble in words, in clothing, in gestures, and in outward appearances; but to be humble and meek of heart.

My writings testify enough that God wishes to enlighten others through this light that He has caused to rise in my soul. I have kept that hidden for a good thirty years, and would have done so even longer, if He did not wish to bring forth new children <note>a metaphor for new converts or spiritual followers born through her ministry</note>. ### On true virtue.

...as I have, and as everyone who reads my writings can have: that God shall bring forth true believers through the lights <note>original: "lichten," referring to divine revelations or spiritual insights</note> He has kindled in my soul. For although these preachers <note>the Mennonite leaders mentioned previously</note> say that I could teach them nothing but what they already know, it is nothing but a conceit they have of knowing all things: for they still lack very much before they could even know what the true rebirth <term>herboorte: a central concept in radical Pietism referring to a total internal transformation by the Holy Spirit</term> is. 

If they knew that well, I believe that some from their communities would strive to obtain it from God; and they would clearly see, through the truths that I present to them, that true rebirth <note>original: "weder-geboorte"</note> does not consist in simple clothes, nor in humble words, nor in remaining tied to their communities. They would thank God that He sends fathers and mothers on earth to give birth to true believers; and they would also see that I have not said that I am one of those same mothers <note>The author frequently uses the metaphor of spiritual motherhood to describe her role in "birthing" new souls into faith</note> out of vain ambition or self-esteem, since I in fact mock the honor of the world and despise its riches and pleasures. 

For since I have known the true good, I have no longer been able to love the false; of which you, my Lord, can bear witness, having associated with me for so long and heard what others have told you about me.

### That it is better to pray than to dispute.

Just as he was never seen in the streets engaging in disputes <note>A reference to Matthew 12:19, describing the Messiah: "He will not quarrel or cry out; no one will hear his voice in the streets."</note>, so I too shall never appear anywhere to do such a thing: for I would never be finished if I were to set myself against so many different opinions <term>opinions; 'gevoelens', literally 'feelings' or 'sentiments', but here referring to theological positions or persuasions</term> as there are concerning Holy Scripture. ### That the disputes [are] by the...

...opinion of everyone; from which presumption <note>original: "vermetelheit"</note> so many errors, so many **Sects** and schisms in **Christendom** have arisen. ## Notice to the Reader.

<image-desc>Decorative drop cap 'I' with floral and foliate scrollwork in a square frame.</image-desc>

I wish, dear Reader, that you might look further into the writings of ANTOINETTE BOURIGNON <note>Antoinette Bourignon (1616–1680) was a controversial Flemish mystic who gained a significant following across Europe by claiming direct communication with God and critiquing the established churches.</note> to enlighten your Soul, if it is open to reason and desires Eternal life. For the more you read her writings, the more your soul shall be enlightened. The teaching of this God-fearing soul is a beauty that wishes to be looked upon closely: she is not painted with cosmetics nor beautiful only in appearance, nor dressed up after the fashion of the World, where men seek nothing but the honor and the reputation of being well-spoken; they often write merely to appear as fine Orators <note>original: "Orateuren"; referring to those trained in formal rhetoric rather than spiritual truth.</note>, and to display their skill and the sharp-wittedness of their spirit. But this soul, enlightened by God, seeks nothing but to obey Him, and simply to declare the Truth of all things without human ulterior motives, so that everyone may draw from it the benefits for their Salvation. Her Kingdom is not of this World, where in truth she finds nothing but crosses, contempt, and persecutions, through the ignorance of men who have only earthly eyes, not seeing the things of the spirit. They would do better to desire and to seek out the continuation of these writings, to see the fountain from which they are drawn, rather than blindly rejecting and despising them as many do, for whom I might well offer the Prayer that Jesus Christ made to his Father at the end of his death, saying:

## Notice to the Reader.

*they know not what they do.* <note>original: "sy en weten niet wat sy doen"; a reference to the words of Jesus on the cross from Luke 23:34.</note> I hear many people who would wish to contradict these writings, some regarding the manner and expressions of the propositions: others regarding certain words that are uncommon in the usage of the Schools <note>The "Schools" refers to formal academic theology and Scholasticism, which Bourignon viewed as overly intellectual and spiritually dry.</note>. But no one can say with truth that her writings contain evil things; they are nothing but slanders and hindrances that the Devil wishes to bring against them, to the end that no one might receive the Divine Truth, which is here so clearly shown that no one can doubt it: unless through malice: seeing as it is so intelligible that the Learned and the ignorant can understand it, by reading these writings attentively, without prejudice of the spirit. Everyone can draw their spiritual benefits from it; therefore I wish to spread them further for the welfare of souls, and to bring them to light as much as will be possible for me; so that those who have found some doubts or concerns through the first writings, may be satisfied by the following ones, which give satisfaction to many reservations <note>original: "achterdenkingen"; meaning second thoughts, suspicions, or lingering doubts.</note> that some might have had in the beginning. One has thought that these writings supported the opinion of the *Roman Catholics*: another, those of *Socinus* <note>Socinians were a sect that denied the Trinity and the full divinity of Christ; Bourignon was often accused of various heresies by her contemporaries.</note>: some, those of the *Reformed*, *Lutherans*, or *Anabaptists*. But one will be able to see in the sequel that this enlightened Soul maintains no other things than the true teaching of *Jesus Christ*, without any partisanship. Therefore I wish to all Christian souls who are desirous of Eternal blessings <note>original: "Eewige goederen"; literally 'eternal goods' or spiritual treasures.</note>,

# FIRST LETTER.
## The Christians of these times have nothing but a Pharisaic Faith.

->*To a trusted friend, explaining with sorrow to what a state Christendom has now fallen.*<-

### SIR.

I give you the freedom to print the letters that I have previously written to the Mennonite Ministers <note>The Mennonites are a group of Anabaptist Christians. Bourignon frequently engaged in heated theological debates with various sects, accusing them of lacking true spiritual life.</note>. I desire that the whole world see what I have written to them: for they speak of it very despicably with few words; so that it is better that one sees openly what I intended to signify with this term, *Mother of the true believers* <note>Bourignon used this title to describe her role as a spiritual guide who "birthed" a new understanding of faith in her followers. Her critics viewed this as a sign of extreme pride or even heresy.</note>. I have explained that sufficiently in the letter against SERARIUS <note>Petrus Serarius (1600–1669) was a well-known Dutch millenarian and theologian who initially supported but later clashed with Bourignon.</note>: But what is not advantageous to their purposes they leave behind, and continue to insist that I have great esteem for myself because of this word *Mother*. It seems to me since Serarius is dead, they now take the trouble to despise me in his place; for which they have much more ability than he, being of a much craftier spirit, more worldly-wise, and more learned. Several people who have been in their company have told me that they said I have good judgment and am also of good life: but that the phrase *Mother of the true believers* testified to a great self-esteem.

**The Christians of these times have nothing,**

Look for a moment, My Lord, at the fine way they act to bring God's lights into contempt: First, they praise me, because they know that my life is known to many, and that they can gain no honor by despising it; but afterwards, they shoot their venom in the conclusion, saying that I have high regard for myself, in order to cause the people who read my writings to feel a loathing. For if a person spoke the best things in the world, and I knew that he was proud <note>original: *hoovaerdig*</note>, I would think that all his fine, beautiful arguments were produced by the devil. Which, being transformed into an Angel of Light <note>A reference to 2 Corinthians 11:14, warning that evil can appear in a holy guise.</note>, can indeed speak good things: but that which comes from the true spirit of God must be good in all parts: not good in one and evil in another. It is flattery <note>original: *vleyerye*</note> to say that my life is good while adding to it that I am proud. A good life cannot coexist with sins. Now, he who considers himself great commits no small act of sin; but he lives in continual sin as long as he remains in self-esteem.

I see clearly that it is not the Mennonites <note>A Protestant group known for their emphasis on plain living and adult baptism; Bourignon frequently clashed with their leadership over matters of spiritual authority.</note> alone who seek to find fault with certain words in my writings, or some reasons and actions in my conduct that are reprehensible: but all the wise, and all those who consider themselves spiritual, do the same. These "wisely-studied" men cannot endure that an uneducated Daughter <note>Bourignon uses the term *ongestudeerde Dochter* (uneducated daughter) as a title of humility to show that her knowledge comes from God rather than university training.</note> should be wise; she who despises their schools and their way of learning through studies, or her

often in the depths of their souls, anything but a hidden hatred toward their neighbor: yet they would not wish to declare the evil of another, even so that sincere hearts might guard themselves against it and not allow themselves to be deceived.

souls who are united in the Spirit of Jesus Christ: these make the true Church. But I seek no interaction nor fellowship with those who call themselves Christians, yet do not have Faith: considering that without it we cannot be Christians.

# The Christians of these times have not,

...[learned]. For if I had ever learned anything through books or **Sermons**, I would still make use of them to learn more; which I do not do at all. My school is **solitude** <term>eensaemheit: a state of physical and spiritual withdrawal used to focus on God</term>; my books are a **pure conscience**; and my master is the **Holy Spirit**. Let those **learned men** say and judge whatever they wish; but they ought not to be angry because God is good, sending them the light of **Truth** to enlighten their souls.

If I spoke of my dreams, of my **visions**, or **revelations**, they would not be strictly obligated to believe me, unless they knew me well: because many of these things are suspicious. For even if a soul is enlightened by God, it can still deceive itself in discerning dreams, visions, or revelations, whenever it becomes mixed with some **personal inclinations** <note>original: "eigen-genegentheden" — self-will or subjective desires that cloud divine perception.</note>, or wishes and desires that things happen just as it has imagined: this corrupts all the revelations that come from God, and deceives us, and causes us to deceive others. 

But in what I say—that one must have **living Faith** to be **saved** <note>original: "Salig" — referring to eternal salvation or being "blessed."</note>, and that one must be possessed by the same **Spirit** as **Jesus Christ** was, in order to be a **Christian**—in that, I can deceive no one. # That one does not light the candle,

### That the Holy Spirit has no need of scrutiny.

You can certainly correct your disciples and students, because you are more advanced in scholarship <note>original: "letteren"; referring here to academic, classical, or theological learning</note> than they; but the Holy Spirit has no need of correction <note>original: "tegen-schrijving"; literally "counter-writing" or contradiction</note>; because he is the Wisdom of God, who gives knowledge to all people: therefore do not touch even a single stroke <note>original: "dát lijntje"; literally "that little line," an idiom meaning do not alter even the smallest part of the text</note>, and do not examine this work to scrutinize it, but rather to draw Blessed lights from it, for the advancement of your own perfection.

It is better to let it stand alone, and it will be enough of a praise unto itself. Those who despise it do not have an upright heart: they may let it pass by without giving it credence. I shall never ask it of them. For the godless cannot approve of good things.

I have heard mention here of various books that are forbidden; and the little that I have heard of their power seems to me to be from the Holy Spirit. # That the Holy Spirit has no need of scrutiny.

...not deny **Thomas à Kempis** <note>original: "Thomas á Kempus"; a 15th-century monk and author of *The Imitation of Christ*, a staple of Christian devotion</note>; but many things are taken out and added to it through new editions, so that the power of the wisdom of the **Holy Spirit** is greatly diminished: and I might well reject what people today approve of. And if I had need to read, I would much rather seek the books that are forbidden or despised, than those they approve; believing that more sincere truths are to be found in what is commonly rejected by the scholars of today; or at least the **Truth** is kept silent or hidden through fear of persecution or the fury of the **godless**, who exert all their power to obstruct the designs of **God**; who, through a final mercy, wishes once more to send His light to people of good will; so that they might emerge from their errors, which are now spread generally throughout the whole world.

I do not know of a single **Religion** that is not full of errors: one in such a manner, the other in another; in one more, in the other less. But all in general, and each in particular, live in a practice directly contrary to the works and teachings of **Jesus Christ**: and they have all, in general, deviated from the living, active **Faith**. There is nothing left in all of **Christendom** but the husk and the appearance <note>original: "schors en den schijn"; metaphors for empty ritual and outward performance without internal spiritual substance</note>. # That the Holy Spirit has no need of scrutiny. 151

...they call one another **deluded spirits** <note>original: "Dwaal-geesten"; a term used in the 17th century for those perceived to be led by a false or wandering spirit rather than the Holy Spirit</note> or **heretics**; meanwhile, one is just as much so as the other. So that the whole of **Christendom** is a complete **Babel** <note>A reference to the biblical Tower of Babel, symbolizing a state of total linguistic and spiritual confusion</note> of confusion, which must soon be broken apart, since the laborers no longer understand one another, and all speak different languages. One must thank **God** that He sends His light of **Truth** once more for the last time. Truly blessed shall he be who accepts it: but few are prepared for it; for instead of examining whether my writings are inspired by the **Holy Spirit**, as I characterize them; some reject them as improper, as coming from a **Daughter** <note>Bourignon refers to herself as a woman; in this period, it was often considered "unseemly" or "improper" for a woman to teach or write on theological matters</note>: others hold them suspect of **heresy**, because they do not agree with the evil practices of modern **Christians**. If this is a **heresy**, then I am quite willing to proceed in it, and hold myself fast to the lights that **God** gives me; even if all people together denied the same, that would bring no harm to my soul. And I have no requirements in this **World**, other than to fulfill the will of **God**; which I have only begun to reveal; hoping to make the same known to you even more; meanwhile, I remain,

->My LORD,<-

->*Your Honour’s very Humble Servant*<-
->**ANTHOINETTE BOURIGNON.**<-

Amsterdam, the 15th of May: 1669.

->The Spirit of God is prudent and reasonable.<-

*To **Mr. de Cort** <note>Christian de Cort (d. 1669) was a Dutch priest and close collaborator of Bourignon who sought to establish a spiritual community with her</note>, a faithful and trusted friend, who asked for advice on necessary matters; he is given counsel, also for the perfection of his soul and the souls of others whom he had under his guidance.*

MY LORD,

I had intended to write no more without great necessity, fearing to commit some uselessness or superfluous repetitions: but I have since seen that there is nothing useless, and that our mutual dealings are always beneficial for certain things; therefore I leave you the freedom to write whenever it pleases you.

# The Spirit of God is prudent and reasonable. 161

## SEVENTH LETTER.

->*To the same person on the same subject.*<-

SIR,

I had written this explanation with the intention of sending it to the little Sons <note>A term Bourignon used for her spiritual followers, whom she viewed as her spiritual children</note>, so that the children might together have received some light; but seeing that they desire no mutual interaction, I did not dare send this to them, fearing whether their conscience might not be strong enough to digest the Truth <note>original: "de Waarheit te verteeren"; the author uses the metaphor of digestion to describe the ability to process difficult spiritual concepts</note>. # to overtake the pious.

with all the gifts and twelve fruits of the **Holy Spirit**. <note>The "twelve fruits" refer to a traditional Christian list derived from Galatians 5:22-23, which includes charity, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, long-suffering, mildness, faith, modesty, continency, and chastity.</note> And even if they seemed to perform miracles; those could be nothing but deceptions, if their souls were not in fact visibly and sensibly possessed by those gifts and fruits: all the more because the **Holy Spirit** cannot keep these things hidden, any more than the **Sun** can hide its brightness. This is what I would well want to make the investigators understand before they set to work, fearing that I might deceive them, as some have done to them with reason; since they demanded signs and miracles from them, just as your <term>Provost</term> <term>original: "Provoost," a high-ranking administrative or judicial official, in this context likely a church magistrate or official overseeing the investigation.</term> has several times demanded in order to believe me: but the consequence that I see from him provides me enough matter to imagine that this question is not asked to benefit his soul through those miracles. 

But much rather to draw from it a reason to bring me harm, and to hand me over into the hands of the **Judges**; given that he would well wish to do such a thing without any cause or object, unless it were for some discourses I have held in the manner of a conversation <note>original: "t'samen-spraak," implying informal or social dialogue rather than formal preaching.</note>, which—even if they had been errors in themselves, as they are not—could not and should not pass for heresies; and even less provide matter for a <term>judicial investigation</term> <term>original: "Rechts-dwingige ondersoekking," a formal legal inquiry or interrogation intended to compel a legal outcome or confession.</term>, devised or proposed by him without reason. For if I have said that there are no longer any true **Christians**; I possess this feeling in my soul, and the **Gospel** confirms this to me, seeing that the lives of men are entirely contradictory <note>That is, contradictory to the teachings of the Gospel.</note>.

# NINETEENTH LETTER.
## That it is necessary to distinguish the good teaching from the bad.

*To a Spiritual Judge, to ask Justice from him regarding false accusations; which one has not been able to reach, because wickedness always wishes to remain hidden, gladly doing its work in secret and not in public.*

### MY LORD,

I desire exceedingly to see the time of your decision, so that I may defend myself against the accusations of the <term>Provost of the Oratorians</term> <note>The Oratorians (the Oratory of Saint Philip Neri) are a Catholic society of priests. If my teaching were an error <note>The original Dutch "dooling" literally means "wandering," often used in a religious context to signify a heresy or a delusion that leads one away from the "right path" of the Church.</note>; it would be a great happiness for me to be able to discover it. # To the Reader.

*This letter was written by Antoinette Bourignon in order to make Pieter Serrarius* <note>Petrus Serrarius (1600–1669) was a prominent Millenarian and mystic in Amsterdam. While he initially supported Bourignon, their relationship soured over theological differences, leading to the "slanders" mentioned here.</note> *recognize his wrongdoing, which he has committed by unjustly burdening her with various slanders. Because of this, she found herself obliged to respond specifically and to make the upright truth public. Otherwise, she feared that many souls might fall into great offense through ignorance, since he has been busy for over six months going from house to house and city to city to diminish her person and writings and bring them into contempt. He even writes to distant countries to people unknown to her, who, answering according to his suggestion, write that her works do not proceed from the Holy Spirit. He joyfully goes about showing these letters to all who follow him, to make them have all the more aversion to the aforementioned writings—which could nevertheless be so very useful and profitable for their salvation* <term>Saligheyt: a state of spiritual blessedness or eternal salvation</term>. *This extensive letter shall then serve to give satisfaction regarding the twelve slanders he has committed against her.*

*She is not inclined to dispute, but only to declare the upright truth of matters, and to demonstrate true virtue from the feigned and imagined; which she clearly does in this following treatise, which has proceeded with sadness from the spirit and hand of this godly soul. For she had previously entreated him with several letters, in all friendship, to be content to stop disputing with her and to remain at peace regarding the conflict of their opinions—telling him that* God *shall be the Judge over it, who will judge in all righteousness and without passion* <note>In this context, "passion" refers to human bias or uncontrolled emotion, which God is presumed to lack.</note>: *but instead of wanting to comply with these so reasonable prayers, he daily attempts to slander this same God-enlightened soul and her writings even more, in such a manner that Christian love* <note>original: "Christelijcke liefde"</note> *obliges her to warn him, so that he does not, in ignorance of such*

And just so are all the other passions more necessary for virtuous souls to work out good than for the <term>ondeugende: vicious or wicked</term>; because the more a vicious soul lives according to her passions, the more sins she commits; and the more virtuous a soul is, the more living and active passions she must have to work righteousness and to maintain—

<meta>This page continues the explanation of the "touchstone" mentioned on the previous page, defining the difference between the Spirit of God and the natural spirit.</meta>

the mark and foundation for distinguishing the spirits: that the Spirit of God has this quality—that He is never busy nor works except for divine and eternal matters, or those that tend toward eternity; and that the natural spirit is never occupied with nor aims for anything other than earthly and temporal things; because everything that belongs to Nature tends toward no other center than time and the earth. And even though man may be a rational animal <note>original: "redelijk dier" — a standard philosophical and theological definition of humanity dating back to Aristotle.</note>, he possesses nothing more than a beast if he remains within his natural spirit. You will perhaps say that man is a much nobler animal than a beast; but it seems to me that he is much lowlier and worse than certain beasts when he remains solely in his nature. For a horse has more strength than he, a bird more lightness, a mouse more alertness, a dog a better sense of smell, and so on with others, down to a little chick, which has no sooner emerged from its shell than it has the ability to feed and clean itself; whereas man would perish from hunger and filth <note>original: "drek" — literally dung or excrement; here referring to the total helplessness of a human infant regarding its own hygiene.</note> if he did not receive assistance from another.

I see here yet another <term>trickery</term> <note>original: "achlistigheid"; implies a subtle, cunning deceit or a trap set by an enemy.</note> of Satan, with which he blinds the spirits of many, making them believe that as soon as they have abandoned evil works to devote themselves to the practice of virtue, they then seek nothing but eternal things, although there is nothing that truly resembles them. For when we seek virtue for the esteem and the <term>pleasure</term> <note>original: "vernoegen"; refers to a sense of self-satisfaction or internal contentment.</note> that we find in it, then we seek only temporal and earthly things, because our pleasure can be nothing other than a passing feeling that belongs to time.

<meta>This page continues Bourignon’s warning against spiritual deception. On the previous page, she discussed the Holy Spirit’s dwelling in the soul and her role as a spiritual mother. Here, she transitions into the cosmic and internal struggle between good and evil, specifically focusing on how the Devil uses "spiritual sweetness" and "false lights" to deceive those who believe they are reborn or holy.</meta>

<page-num>87</page-num>

It might happen <note>The Dutch phrase "'t sou mogen raken" suggests a possibility or a developing situation in spiritual warfare.</note> that Lucifer in this time fights against the Angel: that is to say, the evil against the good, who are few in number; but they shall ultimately remain the strongest and obtain the victory, after they have fought bravely: they shall possess their Souls in patience <note>original: "lijdfaemheit"; a term implying both endurance and peaceful waiting in the face of suffering.</note>, and the evil shall be rooted out. If there were no evil ones other than those who are manifest <note>meaning those whose wickedness is obvious or public.</note>, our time would not be so dangerous, because known evil would not be followed except by those who love evil; and the good would be out of danger. 

But at present, the greatest evils are covered with virtues and disguised with holiness; and the true good is blackened, persecuted, and considered a sin; so that everyone might turn away from the true good. The Devil now has this power over the spirit of men, that he turns them away, by whatever way it may be, from the knowledge of true virtue, and detains them with sensual things and plausible virtues <note>original: "waerschijnelyke deugden"; virtues that look good on the surface but lack a true divine foundation.</note>. 

How many are there of those who believe themselves to have love, or to be reborn, because they sometimes receive certain lights <note>referring to intellectual or spiritual insights.</note>, or have tasted certain spiritual sweetnesses <note>original: "geestelijke soetheden"; a common mystical term for the pleasant emotional feelings or "consolations" felt during prayer or worship.</note>. They believe themselves for this reason to have the spirit of God, and often they have nothing but the natural spirit, holding themselves fast to these lights and sweetnesses in order to rest upon themselves, without foreseeing that the Devil can indeed give the same in great measure, since he is a very bright spirit who has lost nothing of the knowledge of divine mysteries, and can make very spiritual things appear to the understanding of man; yes, give them the knowledge of divine matters and convince them that they come from God and from the Holy Spirit <note>original: "H. Geest."</note>. These are the cunning deceits <note>original: "archlistigheden."</note> with which he the spiritu-

<meta>This page continues Bourignon’s warning about spiritual deception. While the previous page described the Devil’s use of "plausible virtues" to disguise evil, this page explains how he specifically targets the most "spiritual" souls through false enlightenment and emotional religious experiences, concluding with Bourignon's promise to define the characteristics of a "true Christian."</meta>

<page-num>88</page-num>

...seduces the most **spiritual souls**; well knowing that he would not be able to draw them to himself through evil things, he catches them through uncommon lights <note>referring to intellectual or spiritual "flashes" that feel divine but may be deceptive.</note>, making them believe that they are enlightened by **God** and have received his mercy; making them loathe the truth that had rebuked them, in order to keep them held in these **sensible sweetnesses** <note>original: "gevoelige soetheden"; a common term in 17th-century mysticism referring to emotional or physical feelings of religious joy which were often viewed with suspicion by rigorists.</note>. There are many persons who do not wish to hear that they are not **true Christians**; others cannot bear to hear the **Devil** spoken of; others will not hear anything that does not agree with their own feelings; and meanwhile they claim to have the light and the **graces of God**, which I cannot understand, and in this, either I or they must surely be deceived. 

For if they were enlightened by **God**, they would recognize that they are not **true Christians**; and also that the **Devil** has great dominion over the spirit of man; just as they would also always hold their own feelings suspect, wishing to understand those of others, to know if they might be better than their own. For this reason I pity them, and could not help them except by uncovering for them the identifying marks <note>original: "merkteekenen"; signs or criteria used to evaluate spiritual authenticity.</note> by which to know a **true Christian**, and the errors in which those who bear the name of **Christians** currently find themselves; so that they might recognize by these whether they are **true Christians**, whether they labor for the future <note>meaning the eternal life or the coming Kingdom of God.</note>, or whether they sit in the delusions and the deceptions of **Satan**; to which end I shall apply myself at the first opportunity. Meanwhile I remain,

->Sir,<-

->Your very humble Servant,<-

->**A. B.**<-

From **Amsterdam**,
June 21,
1668.
